chunks: And Ali ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Abu Hamza from Abu Baseer, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali saying:
By Allah, you will be distinguished, by Allah you will be purified, by Allah you will be sifted like the chaff is sifted from the wheat.

key_terms.الزَّوَانُ: Chaff (the husks of grain separated from the wheat)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Shia being sifted like chaff from wheat during the occultation?
ai.summary: In the context of the Minor Occultation, Imam al-Baqir uses the agricultural metaphor of sifting chaff from wheat to describe the inevitable purification of the Shia community. This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani, highlights the theological significance of the 'Ghayba' as a period of divine testing that distinguishes true adherents from those of weaker faith, ensuring the preservation of authentic tradition.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi al-Abbasi from Ahmad bin Muhammad from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Ziyad from Ali bin Abu Hamza that Abu Baseer had said: “I heard Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) saying: “
By Allah, you are going to be tested, clarified and sifted like sifting out the Zu’an from wheat.”
